aspects.says: On 2.1.7 a deadline is measured from the TIMESTAMP IncomingListener stores on arrival, so queue time counts, and work the terminal no longer waits for is not done.
basis: section:13.2.1 The 2.1.7 Way to a Deadline: Compare the Arrival Time With the Clock

aspects.says: jPOS 3 changes the log, metrics, TLS, XML and CMF defaults, and a migration is proved by running the flows through the real components on the target version.
basis: section:13.5 Logs, Metrics and Security Defaults Change What Operations Sees
section:13.6 A Migration Is Proved by Running Your Tests on the New Line
aspects.reason: jPOS 3 behaviour that the 2.1.7 runtime of the practices cannot show, and a procedure rather than a checkable fact

aspects.says: Commit order decides whether SendResponse answers before Close removes TX, and QMUX 2.1.7 returns null after the timeout on a dead link instead of throwing.
basis: section:13.3 The Same Descriptor Can Behave Differently on the Two Lines

aspects.says: TransactionManager.getContext() is null on a callback's thread in 2.1.7 and removed in 3.0.2, so the Context is passed explicitly.
basis: section:13.4 Code That Finds Its Transaction Through a Thread-Local Breaks on Both Lines

aspects.says: jPOS 3.x is the tip and 2.x the tail, which gets critical fixes only; jpos.org describes jPOS 3, which needs Java 23 or later.
basis: section:13.1 jPOS 3 Is the Tip, 2.1.x Is the Tail, and jpos.org Describes the Tip
aspects.reason: release facts and a choice of line, with nothing a graded run on 2.1.7 can observe

aspects.says: 2.1.7 silently ignores jPOS 3 descriptor options it doesn't read (participant max-time, timeout, requires/provides, QMUX pcode), so a pcode override covers its whole MTI class.
basis: section:13.2 A jPOS 3 Descriptor Deploys on 2.1.7, and What 2.1.7 Doesn't Read Does Nothing
